start_here: Say to your AI: "Use mflux on my computer: make an image from a text prompt on your own Mac with Apple silicon, with "A puffin standing on a cliff"." It reads the row, installs mflux if it is missing, runs it and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: mflux is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on what it is handed there.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use mflux on my computer: make an image from a text prompt on your own Mac with Apple silicon, with "A puffin standing on a cliff"." It reads the row with do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:mflux-community-mflux"}.

2. It checks that uv, Apple silicon Mac are on your computer, and if mflux is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux.git ; uv tool install --upgrade mflux.
3. It runs the row's command: mflux-generate-z-image-turbo --prompt "A puffin standing on a cliff" --steps 9
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. The site you asked through runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: mflux: an image of a puffin on your Mac
worked_examples.ask: Use mflux on my computer: make an image from a text prompt on your own Mac with Apple silicon, with "A puffin standing on a cliff".
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json: tool:github:mflux-community-mflux runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got mflux in, the command line: mflux-generate-z-image-turbo --prompt "A puffin standing on a cliff" --steps 9
worked_examples.hands_back: mflux prints its steps as it generates and saves the image as image.png in the folder it ran in; the first run also downloads the model it uses.
